rows.boundary: Motivation and publication context; not executable requirements.

rows.title: Minimal fix/mix nucleus
rows.boundary: The explicit recursive Interaction calculus has a total finite observer, an unbounded inductive operational semantics, soundness/completeness, stable observations, divergence correspondence and related-carrier transfer. It supports heterogeneous inherited carriers and delayed values. Shared unsafe thunks remain an alternate runtime; arbitrary Scheme programs are outside the stated calculus. Call-by-need caches carry evaluation proofs indexed by the exact program; completed source errors are shared. Active cycles are separate runtime diagnostics. Mutable writes reset the cache and advance the generation.

Corrupt fixture identity and incomplete/duplicate/mismatched receipts fail closed. Differential examples do not establish whole-language equivalence.

rows.boundary: Checked errors and pending recursive observations are distinct. The operational semantics characterizes both completed errors and divergence; finite budget exhaustion alone is not a divergence proof.

rows.boundary: Both concrete source alternatives implemented: shared AVL cells and prototype/key-list pairs. Typed homogeneous/dependent families and explicit key-slot override policy; no universal representation equivalence theorem.

rows.title: Unified instance/prototype objects
rows.boundary: Typed retained prototype/value pairs and later extension coexist with safe recursive C3 plans and fresh shared instances. Slot reads preserve final-self requests and carry evaluation proofs for the exact plan; arbitrary Scheme closures are outside the declared value universe.

rows.title: Multiple inheritance
rows.boundary: Certified C3 is connected to actual typed object slot composition and to the safe dynamic recursive object path. Any source-style graph derivation gives exactly the same order and object observation. For finite DAGs with rank bounded by the production graph-size fuel and strictly decreasing on declared edges, complete cached/uncached batch outcomes agree for arbitrary depth and root lists, including missing-parent and inconsistent-merge errors. Validation and existing cyclic/error controls remain. The general cyclic-graph cached/reference outcome theorem is not asserted. C4 remains a separately selectable policy with its own extensions.

rows.title: Prototype as extensible meta-object
rows.boundary: Function/supers/precedence are overridable slots of first-class metadata objects; string registry identifiers replace recursive dynamic identity. Parent caches are caller metadata, not ancestry-certified C4 orders.

rows.title: Further feature overview
rows.boundary: Points to advanced extensions; evaluate the concrete Appendix B constructions separately.

rows.title: Classes as descriptor prototypes
rows.boundary: Static class prototypes compose descriptors over typed carriers. Dynamic class prototypes compose descriptors in the recursive Value universe; runtime factories and actual C3 field admission execute. Arbitrary Scheme values and closures are outside the declared universe.

rows.title: I/O validation
rows.boundary: JSON/text/byte and slot refinement controls; Lean wire format, not Scheme binary compatibility.

rows.title: Simple type repertoire
rows.boundary: Static typed descriptors and a recursive dynamic Value universe coexist. Dynamic contracts cover primitives, ranges, lists, dictionaries, objects, named recursive types and first-class descriptors. Current registry identity is required; budget exhaustion is an error. Lean Int/strings replace Scheme number/sexp carriers.

rows.title: Parameterized descriptors
rows.boundary: Runtime DescriptorFactory consumes dynamic descriptors or ordinary values and registers fresh descriptors with unique explicit identities. ListOf, DictionaryOf, FunctionOf, ObjectOf, range, union and intersection constructors execute. Duplicate identities and invalid/missing descriptor parameters are rejected. Arbitrary closure serialization and universal automation are excluded.

rows.title: Self-describing elaborate descriptors
rows.boundary: Runtime descriptors expose contract constructors/arguments and open metadata in the same dynamic value universe. Functions/descriptors use explicit registry identities. Function calls check input and output refinements, with kernel admission soundness; function membership checks callability, not universal behavioral properties. Existing finite catalogs/codecs/generated updates retain their stated scope; closure serialization and unspecified universal automation are not claimed. Dynamic slot/schema catalogs now generate defaults, inspection, ordered updates and structural text/byte codecs. Catalogs describe and reconstruct themselves. Wire admission checks every nested function/descriptor identity in the current registry and returns a kernel Accepted proof. Actual lazy C3 object fields retain evaluation receipts and enter the same descriptor/wire gate. Generated codec round trips are executable controls, not a general codec inverse theorem.

rows.title: Classes/typeclasses correspondence
rows.boundary: TypedValue and descriptors do not prove an automated bidirectional transformation between typeclasses and prototype classes.

rows.title: Pure linearity and mutable/functional interaction
rows.boundary: Pure storage, mutable hash identities and consumed linear references share one declared slot transition. write_pureSlot and composition associativity are kernel laws. Tests compare pure/mutable/linear observations, alias visibility and persistent snapshots. Linear failure preserves the old reference; mutable failure retains prior writes. IO effect correspondence is exercised, not an unrestricted kernel IO refinement theorem. Mutable force results retain their exact immutable snapshot and kernel evaluation proof; each slot write clears memo entries and increments the generation under the same mutex.

rows.title: Simplified mutable prototype protocol
rows.boundary: fix!/mix! allocate one fresh mutex-protected hash identity, run parent before child, update each slot with one table insertion, capture inherited syntax lazily and resolve final-self requests on later reads. No topology rebuild is needed per write. Failure retains prior writes and skips subsequent child mutations. Snapshot and consuming-state conversions execute. No machine-level O(1) time or allocation bound is asserted. Optional safe forcing shares completed values/errors and diagnoses active cycles. All cached results are invalidated on mutation; snapshot-indexed receipts prevent reuse in a changed program.

rows.title: Cache invalidation alternatives
rows.boundary: Explicit dependency contracts and proof reuse are local extensions; no language-wide purity/effect inference or arbitrary-body invalidation.

rows.boundary: lensGen implements getter/setter/wrapper and skew-focus laws exist. The paper itself calls full generalized prototypes future work; no claim that all such semantics are closed.

rows.title: Appendix C type notation
rows.boundary: Lean dependent types replace expository notation; no formal source row/subtyping calculus translation is established.

rows.title: Appendix D fixed-point functions
rows.boundary: Shared/rebuilding unsafe thunks remain executable alternatives. The safe recursive calculus supplies sound/complete finite observation, unbounded return/error semantics, divergence characterization, and least-information refinement against any fixed observation. Concrete shared-thunk parity is tested; no arbitrary unsafe-thunk equivalence is claimed. The safe shared evaluator provides proven memo receipts, cold-slot laziness, cached errors and active-path cycle diagnostics; concurrent instance reads serialize on a mutex.

rows.title: Appendix E code minimalism
rows.boundary: Scheme cons-cell/character counts are illustrative, not Lean size or semantic requirements.
